entities.summary:
Aemilius Asper was a prominent Latin grammarian who likely lived in the 1st or late 2nd century AD. He was a key figure in the development of Latin language and literature, particularly in the realm of grammar and rhetoric. His work had a lasting impact on the education system and literary circles of the Roman Empire.

As a grammarian, Asper was particularly interested in the rules of Latin syntax and the study of classical texts. He is known to have written several treatises on these subjects, which were widely read and studied by scholars throughout the Roman Empire.

Asper's contributions to the field of Latin language and literature were significant, and he is still studied and referenced by scholars today. His work on grammar and rhetoric has had a lasting impact on the education system and literary circles of the Roman Empire, and his legacy continues to be felt in the study of classical languages and literature.
